complete_original_paragraphs.literal: When DRX is in use the UE shall be able to identify a new detectable FS3 intra-frequency cell within the cell identification time Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX, where the cell identification time of a cell shall include detection of the cell and additionally performing a single measurement with measurement period of Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX, where:.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: When DRX is in use the UE shall be able to identify a new detectable FS3 intra-frequency cell within the cell identification time Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX, where the cell identification time of a cell shall include detection of the cell and additionally performing a single measurement with measurement period of Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX, where:.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX is the intra-frequency period for cell identification as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX is the intra-frequency period for cell identification as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX is the intra-frequency period for measurements as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-2,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX is the intra-frequency period for measurements as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-2,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: TDMTC_periodicity is the discovery signal measurement timing configuration periodicity of higher layer,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: TDMTC_periodicity is the discovery signal measurement timing configuration periodicity of higher layer,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: L is the number of configured discovery signal occasions during ON DURATION and which are not available during Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX for cell identification at the UE due to the absence of the necessary radio signals from the cell,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: L is the number of configured discovery signal occasions during ON DURATION and which are not available during Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX for cell identification at the UE due to the absence of the necessary radio signals from the cell,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: M is the number of configured discovery signal occasions during ON DURATION and which are not available during Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX for the measurements at the UE due to the absence of the necessary radio signals from the cell.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: M is the number of configured discovery signal occasions during ON DURATION and which are not available during Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX for the measurements at the UE due to the absence of the necessary radio signals from the cell.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1: Intra-frequency cell identification requirements under operation with frame structure 3
complete_original_paragraphs.final: Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1: Intra-frequency cell identification requirements under operation with frame structure 3

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: NOTE 1:	Discovery signal occasion duration (ds-OccasionDuration) is 1 ms.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: NOTE 1:	Discovery signal occasion duration (ds-OccasionDuration) is 1 ms.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: NOTE 2:	The requirements for measurement bandwidth ≥25 RB are optional.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: NOTE 2:	The requirements for measurement bandwidth ≥25 RB are optional.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: NOTE 3:	k=2 when the measurement gaps configured for inter-frequency measurements in DMTC occasions or for inter-frequency RSSI measurements in RMTC occasions on a carrier with frame structure 3 overlap with some but not all DMTC occasions of the measured cell during ON DURATION; otherwise, k=1, e.g., when measurement gaps configured for inter-frequency measurements on a carrier with frame structure 3 do not overlap with DMTC occasions of the measured cell during ON DURATION or when the UE does not require the measurement gaps for the inter-frequency measurements. The requirements apply, provided that the inter-frequency measurement gap pattern does not overlap with all DMTC occasions of the measured cell.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: NOTE 3:	k=2 when the measurement gaps configured for inter-frequency measurements in DMTC occasions or for inter-frequency RSSI measurements in RMTC occasions on a carrier with frame structure 3 overlap with some but not all DMTC occasions of the measured cell during ON DURATION; otherwise, k=1, e.g., when measurement gaps configured for inter-frequency measurements on a carrier with frame structure 3 do not overlap with DMTC occasions of the measured cell during ON DURATION or when the UE does not require the measurement gaps for the inter-frequency measurements. The requirements apply, provided that the inter-frequency measurement gap pattern does not overlap with all DMTC occasions of the measured cell.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: NOTE 4:	The requirements apply, provided that L is such that the intra-frequency cell identification period Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX does not exceed 72*k* Max{TDMTC_periodicity, DRX cycle length}.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: NOTE 4:	The requirements apply, provided that L is such that the intra-frequency cell identification period Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX does not exceed 72*k* Max{TDMTC_periodicity, DRX cycle length}.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: A cell shall be considered detectable when the following conditions are met during the discovery signal occasions which are available during Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX:
complete_original_paragraphs.final: A cell shall be considered detectable when the following conditions are met during the discovery signal occasions which are available during Tidentify_intra_FS3_DRX:

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: -	RSRP related side conditions given in Section 9.1.18.2 are fulfilled for a corresponding Band,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: -	RSRP related side conditions given in Section 9.1.18.2 are fulfilled for a corresponding Band,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: -	RSRQ related side conditions given in Section 9.1.18.3 are fulfilled for a corresponding Band,
complete_original_paragraphs.final: -	RSRQ related side conditions given in Section 9.1.18.3 are fulfilled for a corresponding Band,

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: -	SCH_RP is according to Annex B.2.12 for a corresponding Band and SCH Ês/Iot is according to Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: -	SCH_RP is according to Annex B.2.12 for a corresponding Band and SCH Ês/Iot is according to Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-1.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: If higher layer filtering is used, an additional cell identification delay can be expected.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: If higher layer filtering is used, an additional cell identification delay can be expected.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: In the RRC_CONNECTED state the measurement period for intra-frequency measurements is Tmeasure_ intra_FS3_CRS_DRX as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-2, when DRX is in use. The UE shall be capable of p performing RSRP and RSRQ measurements for 3 identified intra-frequency cells, and the UE physical layer shall be capable of reporting measurements to higher layers within the measurement period of Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX.
complete_original_paragraphs.final: In the RRC_CONNECTED state the measurement period for intra-frequency measurements is Tmeasure_ intra_FS3_CRS_DRX as shown in Table 8.11.2.1.1.2-2, when DRX is in use. The UE shall be capable of p performing RSRP and RSRQ measurements for 3 identified intra-frequency cells, and the UE physical layer shall be capable of reporting measurements to higher layers within the measurement period of Tmeasure_intra_FS3_CRS_DRX.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: The SFTD measurement reporting delay is defined as the time between a command that will trigger an SFTD measurement report and the point when the UE starts to transmit the measurement report over the air interface. This requirement assumes that the measurement report is not delayed by other RRC signalling on the DCCH. This measurement reporting delay excludes a delay uncertainty resulted when inserting the measurement report to the TTI of the uplink DCCH. The delay uncertainty is: 2 x TTIDCCH. This measurement reporting delay excludes any delay caused by no UL resources for UE to send the measurement report. When the UE is configured to perform SRS carrier-based switching, an additional delay can be expected.

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: Specifications and test procedures for FR1 and FR2 follow two distinct paths in 3GPP. FR1 uses omni-directional antennas in a non-array configuration and relies on conducted test methods as baseline approach. While digital beamforming is provisioned in the standard, it is not vital for the operation of a UE in sub-7GHz region of the spectrum. On the other hand, FR2 uses antenna arrays and relies on beamforming to compensate for higher pathloss at mm-wave frequencies.

The situation is less clear with intermediate spectrum between FR1 and FR2. At the lower end of the spectrum (immediate vicinity of FR1), antenna arrays can be prohibitively large and may not be required after all. On the other hand, at the higher end of the spectrum (immediate vicinity of FR2), antenna arrays, OTA test methods, and beamforming may be the only option due to higher path loss and unavailability of RF connectors and other components.
To address these questions and other technology feasibility studies, 7-24GHz frequency range is broken down into 3 smaller sub-ranges as follows [1]:

Receiver sensitivity is one of the most fundamental performance specifications on the receive side and is defined as the lowest received signal level which can be successfully demodulated by the receiver for a specified BER. For conducted sensitivity, the received signal level is measured at the antenna connector. For radiated sensitivity, the received signal level is measured as the mean incident power in the plane wave with a given polarization. Either way, the following equation can be used to define the receiver sensitivity:

Where LIM is implementation loss in systems using antenna arrays and beamforming. For example, distribution network and phase shifters are accounted for through LIM. Note that since conducted sensitivity is measured at the antenna connector, GAnt=LIM=0.

Given the fact that TDD is the preferred duplex method for frequency bands above 3GHz [2], it is safe to assume that all 3 sub-ranges will also rely on this duplex method to avoid interference between transmitter and receiver.

Receiver architecture (including antenna system) plays an important role in calculating system NF. At higher frequencies, Active Antenna Systems (AAS) with antenna arrays and beamforming networks become necessary to compensate for higher path loss and maintain similar link performance as lower frequencies [4]. Besides, at higher frequencies, AAS are integrated with the rest of the receive chain in a way that antenna connectors are no longer available.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: It is well known that phase noise degrades at a rate of ~6dB/octave with frequency. Since in a zero-IF architecture, RF LO will be at a higher frequency compared to a super-heterodyne architecture, it will have higher phase noise and will contribute more to overall system noise. Note that IF LO in a super-heterodyne architecture will have its own phase noise contribution. But degradation of phase noise with frequency combined with other issues related to generating RF LO for zero-IF architecture at higher frequencies, generally makes RF+IF down-conversion a more attractive choice at higher frequencies. On the other hand, a super-heterodyne architecture, even in the absence of any jammers in the image band, suffers from image band noise and requires either filtering before the first down conversion or image-reject downconverter designs.

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: Title:	TP to TR38.831: FR2 UE architectures for DL Intra-band CA BW Enhancement
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: Title:	TP to TR38.831: FR2 UE architectures for DL Intra-band CA BW Enhancement

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: RAN4 established that the DL CA BW enhancement feature for Rel-16 would be captured as a UE capability to support DL-only coverage spectrum [1]. ‘DL Coverage Spectrum’ here means the range of DL frequencies that can be populated with a DL CC in CA mode
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: RAN4 established that the DL CA BW enhancement feature for Rel-16 would be captured as a UE capability to support DL-only coverage spectrum [1]. ‘DL Coverage Spectrum’ here means the range of DL frequencies that can be populated with a DL CC in CA mode

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: The agreement was based partly on the study of practical UE architecture choices to enable this feature [2]. In this contribution, we propose a TP to TR to capture the UE architecture study.
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: The agreement was based partly on the study of practical UE architecture choices to enable this feature [2]. In this contribution, we propose a TP to TR to capture the UE architecture study.

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: 4.3	FR2 UE requirements for contiguous intra-band DL CA for aggregated bandwidth larger than 1200 MHz
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: 4.3	FR2 UE requirements for contiguous intra-band DL CA for aggregated bandwidth larger than 1200 MHz

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: Enhanced DL CA aggregated BW is gated by:
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: Enhanced DL CA aggregated BW is gated by:

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: DL data pipe size in the digital domain
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: DL data pipe size in the digital domain

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: Signal-handling bandwidth of the ‘front end’, which include RF electronics, ADCs, filters, etc. This parameter is identical to frequency separation, which is defined as the frequency span between the lower edge of the lowest component carrier and the upper edge of the highest component carrier that a UE can support simultaneously.
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: Signal-handling bandwidth of the ‘front end’, which include RF electronics, ADCs, filters, etc. This parameter is identical to frequency separation, which is defined as the frequency span between the lower edge of the lowest component carrier and the upper edge of the highest component carrier that a UE can support simultaneously.

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: DL data pipe size enhancement is left to UE implementation. UE frequency separation enhancement is addressed in the UE architecture study in the next subsection. The following assumptions apply:
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: DL data pipe size enhancement is left to UE implementation. UE frequency separation enhancement is addressed in the UE architecture study in the next subsection. The following assumptions apply:

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: The UE’s UL electronics (frequency separation ability) and data handling capacity (‘data pipe’) are left untouched while the DL CA capability is enhanced
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: The UE’s UL electronics (frequency separation ability) and data handling capacity (‘data pipe’) are left untouched while the DL CA capability is enhanced

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: The UE’s DL CA frequency spectrum coverage, i.e the band where a UE can support placing DL CCs is contiguous. This assumption does not mean DL CA must also be contiguous.
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: The UE’s DL CA frequency spectrum coverage, i.e the band where a UE can support placing DL CCs is contiguous. This assumption does not mean DL CA must also be contiguous.

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: All DL CCs have the same AoA
cover_first30_paragraphs.final: All DL CCs have the same AoA

cover_first30_paragraphs.literal: In [1], we identified some RF requirements that would require special consideration for FR2 inter-band CA. In this contribution we propose a TP to capture REFSENS assumptions for inter-band CA. The proposal is crafted to be agnostic of whether the gNBs for the participating bands are co-located or not.

complete_original_paragraphs.literal: For inter-band carrier aggregation, the requirement applies per band, with one component carrier per operating band. The inter-band requirement applies with common AoA for all active component carriers. The uplink is assigned to one band. The throughput for each component carrier shall be ≥ 95 % of the maximum throughput of the reference measurement channels as specified in Annexes A.2.3.2 and A.3.3.2 (with one sided dynamic OCNG Pattern OP.1 TDD for the DL-signal as described in Annex A.5.2.1) with peak reference sensitivity for each carrier specified in Table 7.3.2.1-1. The requirement on each component carrier applies when the power in the component carriers in other bands correspond to their respective EIS levels for that AoA and test condition. The requirement is verified with the test metric of EIS (Link=Beam peak search grids, Meas=Link Angle).

source_summary:
Remove EN-DC combinations 7(UL)_n78(DL), 41(UL)_n77(DL), and 41(UL)_n78(DL) from Table 7.3B.2.3.2-1 and Table 7.3B.2.3.2-2.
Void NOTE 7 in Table 7.3B.2.3.2-1.
Change n79(UL)_11(DL) note index from 3 to 4 in Table 7.3B.2.3.2-1.
Remove empty rows in Table 7.3B.2.3.2-1 and Table 7.3B.2.3.2-2.

The EN-DC combinations that involve 41(UL)_n77(DL) and 41(UL) and n78(DL) had the harmonic mixing MSD converted to cross band noise MSD by mistake. The chronology is as follows:

RAN4#85:       R4-1714012 Introduction to band combination
RAN4#86:       R4-1801993 TP on TR37.863-01-01 for DC_41A_n77A
RAN4#86-Bis: R4-1805631 TP on TR37.863-01-01 for DC_41A_n78A
RAN4#87:       R4-1806769 TP on TR37.863-01-01 for DC_41A_n77A and
                        41A_n78A. Conversion error happens here

The following additional changes are needed to complete the removal and correction of MSD.

Based on the noise quantities in R4-1714012 and re-calculating MSD based on 3GPP REFSENS, we add a section for cross-band noise MSD in Table 7.3B.2.3.4-1 and UL configuration of aggressor band in Table 7.3B.2.3.4-2.

members.name: R4-1913224 CR on UL MIMO correction of reference planes (Cat.F).doc

source_summary:
Where it says “UE with two transmit connectors” and “ UE supporting UL MIMO” is replaced with “For UE configured for two logical antenna ports” and in the following the sentence “of sum of powers fromall transmit antenna connectors” is also added instead of “each antenna connector”. 
For transmit signal quality, “each antenna connector” is kept. 
“The requirements shall be met with UE configuration specified in subsection 6.2D.1.” is added and in some cases reference to Table 6.2D.1-2 is removed since table alone is not explicit. 
New section headings “6.4D.2.0 General” and “6.5D.0 General” are added to remove the hanging paragraph
“Codebook index” changed to “TPMI index”

members.name: R4-1913235 UE antenna gain range 38.133 CR Rel-15.docx

source_summary:
Introduce a new subclause specifying the allowable antenna gain range of the UE. The new subclause has been placed next to the subclauses which already specify for example gain difference between rough and fine beams.

The values for UE power class 3 have been taken from the agreement recorded in R4-1912670, Ad Hoc minutes for Rel-15 NR RRM at RAN4#92bis. Values for other power classes are currently FFS.

frozen_records.summaryOfChange:
Update the test parameters in Test case A.7.7.1.1:
Introduce time periods T1 and T2, to test Relative reporting accuracy between 2 levels on the same cell
Change the angle of arrival to Rx beam peak, and use 24RBs, to allow enough SS-RSRP dB range
Use time period T1 with 2 cells, and maximise the SS-RSRP difference when measuring Relative reporting accuracy with 2 cells on the same frequency. Set Io as close as possible to the maximum value and use Noc and Es, to give controlled Es/Iot.
Time period T2 uses Cell 1 and Cell 2 SSB_RP as low as possible, while keeping Es/Iot at minimum value
dB values are set according to the side conditions for the UE power class and operating band under test
Es/Noc is removed from the general parameters table, as it is covered in the OTA related test parameters table
Original Reference channels SR.3.1 TDD, CR.3.1 TDD and CCR.3.1 TDD can be used, so the [ ] added in R4-1912773 are not needed. The OCNG has been changed from OP.1 to OP.3, a new OCNG for unused REs in same BW as RMC (here, 24RBs)
Propagation conditions and Antenna configuration specified per cell

frozen_records.summaryOfChange:
Clarification of known TCI state definition 
It is agreed in RAN4#91 (R4-1907305 ad hoc minutes);
Agreement:
The known TCI state is defined by the time from the latest measurement resource for the TCI to when TCI activation command is received, 
If the period is less than X, the TCI state is considered as known. Otherwise the TCI state is considered as unknown.
Before when TCI activation command is received
L1 RSRP measurement for the RS to which the target TCI is QCLed with should be reported
The QCLed condition shall be specified in the specification.

Update to definition of first SSB to clarify that first SSB should be used to derive timing for target TCI state
Update to define values for different QCL types
Update to condition for RRC based TCI switch delay requirements
Corrections to sub-section titles

source_summary:
The following changes are made:
New limits for BS type 1-O and BS type 2-O are introduced, where the limits are based on Category B TX spurious emission limits. 
For BS Type 2-O, it is also clarified that the OTA RX spurious emissions requirement shall apply during the transmitter OFF period only.
Since the step frequencies in subclause 9.7.5.3.2.3 are referenced, the table with step frequencies is updated to cover bands relevant for both Category A and B.
A temporary note for stricter limits in regional regulation is added.

__MACOSX/._R4-1913682 CR on introducing inter-frequency without measurement gap (9.1.5,9.1.6,9.3.1,9.3.4,9.3.5)-v4.docx

source_summary:
Clause 9.1.5 introduce carrier-specific scaling factor for inter-frequency measurement without gap
Clause 9.1.6 introduce inter-frequency measurement for transitions from outside gaps to within gaps or vice versa
Clause 9.3.1 introduce the definition of inter-frequency without measurement gap
Clause 9.3.4 change the clause title to “inter frequency measurements with measurement gaps”, and add sub cluase 9.3.4.1 and 9.3.4.2
Clause 9.3.5 new clause for inter frequency measurements without measurement gaps, including cell identification, measurement period and scheduling availability of UE during inter-frequency measurements

                        41A_n78A. Conversion error happens here

cells_literal:
Add notes at the corresponding clauses.
 6.4.2	Transmit modulation quality and 6.4D.2 Transmit modulation quality 
for UL MIMO
     UE shall not be allowed to report parameter 3300 and 3301 via 
txDirectCurrentLocation IE.
 
 6.4A.2.3	Transmit modulation quality for inter-band CA
     In a case if the parameter 3300 or 3301 is reported from UE via 
txDirectCurrentLocation IE, verdict of carrier leakage measurement shall 
be inconclusive, and the RF correction with regard to the carrier leakage 
and IQ image is omitted during the calculation of transmit modulation 
quality.

members.name: R4-1913963_Introduction of LTE-A inter-band CA for x bands (x=3,4,5) DL with 2 bands UL into TS36.101.docx

source_summary:
This CR is implemented with the current version 16.3.0 of TS 36.101 and all changes have been added in this CR.

The following operating bands were completed in RAN4 #92Bis and these completed operating bands were included in enodorsed R4-1911438.

New 3 bands DL with 2 bands UL CA band combinations from RAN4 #92Bis are introduced to Table 5.6A.1-2A: E-UTRA CA configurations and bandwidth combination sets defined for inter-band CA (three bands)

New 4 bands DL with 2 bands UL CA band combinations from RAN4 #92Bis are introduced to Table 5.6A.1-2b: E-UTRA CA configurations and bandwidth combination sets defined for inter-band CA (four bands)

For some CA band combinations with IMD problems, agreed MSD exception requirements are defined in 7.3.1A from RAN4 #92Bis meeting.

Agreed MSD value for CA 2A-13A-66A-66B/CA 13A-66A has been missing from RAN4 #90Bis and needs to be added to TS 36.101.

When the band 46 has self-interference problems with operating dual uplink CA, the requirements of Refesens (Band 46) do not need to be applied in exclusion zone.
 
The following operating bands have been completed in RAN4 #93 meeting.

New 3 bands DL with 2 bands UL CA band combinations from RAN4 #93 are introduced to Table 5.6A.1-2A: E-UTRA CA configurations and bandwidth combination sets defined for inter-band CA (three bands)


New 4 bands DL with 2 bands UL CA band combinations from RAN4 #93 are introduced to Table 5.6A.1-2b: E-UTRA CA configurations and bandwidth combination sets defined for inter-band CA (four bands)

source_summary:
Clause 6.2D.1:
1. remove the ambiguity on applicability of the requirements when TPMI = 0 is sent:  requirements for both single-layer and dual-layer transmission is specified with two ports configured.
2. specify the fall-back single-antenna port behaviour: at least PC3 performance must be met when PUSCH is scheduled for single port transmission by DCI 0_0 (verified per connector)
3. add a requirement that full power shall according to the power class shall be delivered when PUSCH is scheduled by DCI 0_1 and the UE is configured with a single antenna port following 38.213.

The behavour according to items 2 and 3 are specified in the remaining subclauses of 6.2D.

source_summary:
Subclause 5.5B.4.1: EN-DC band combinations for n91, n92, n93 and n94 with ULSUP-TDM listed.

Subclause 6.3: requirements on unwanted emissions is specified for any overlap between EUTRA and NR slots in TDM operation. 

Subclause 6.3B.1.1: a guard period of ±3 s centred at the end of the preceding slot/symbol is introduced in the time masks for ULSUP-TDM to make clear the conditions under which these core requirements apply. The duration of the guard period corresponds to a collocated case with MRTD = 3 s.

Subclause 6.5B.3.3.2: spurious emission requirements specified for the EN-DC band combinations introduced.

The modified time masks for ULSUP-TDM do not impact UEs supporting SUL band combinations implemented in accordance with the Rel-15 version of this specification (in which there is no guard period).

members.name: R4-1914424 Correction to BWP switching delay.docx

source_summary:
Clarify that DL slot n (the slot UE receive DCI or inactivity timer expires) is the n-th slot with SCS before BWP switching.

Clarify that the index of slot in which UE shall transmit/receive on the new BWP is given in slots with SCS after BWP switching

Clarify that for DCI-based or timer-based BWP switching UE shall transmit/receive on the new BWP in slot n∙SCSnewSCSold+TBWPswitchDelay∙SCSnewmax SCSold,SCSnew .

The description of interruption duration for DCI-based BWP switching is changed to “The UE is not required to transmit UL signals or receive DL signals during time duration between the end of DL slot n according to SCSold and the beginning of DL slot nnew according to SCSnew  on the cell where DCI-based BWP switch occurs”

Clarify that for RRC-based BWP switching UE shall transmit/receive on the new BWP in slot ceil(n*SCSnew/SCSold) + (TRRCProcessingDelay+TBWPswitchDelayRRC)/NR slot length (according to SCSnew)

Some format typos are corrected.

members.name: R4-1914676 draftCR for 38.104 Performance requirements for FR2 PUSCH 2T2R 16QAM V1.docx

source_summary:
This draftCR changes the performance requirement tables for FR2, to implement the following agreements:

[R4-1910006]:
Agree to replace all the existing FR2 2T2R requirements with MCS 16 by MCS12 in TS 38.104 and TS 38.141-2.
Reuse the agreed simulation assumptions for FR2 2T2R cases with MCS 16 by referring to Slide#6 in [R4-1907241].

[R4-1912722]:
The PUSCH FR2 2T2R with MCS 12 requirements are applicable from Rel-16.

Agenda item: 9.18.2

source_summary:
Add new section for interruption length requirements for direct SCell activation. The interruption length is 1ms for inter-band CA and 5ms for intra-band CA.
In RAN4#92, some companies mentioned that the interruption length should consider UE doing both SCell addition and activation/hibernation, so we propose the interruption length is 2ms for inter-band case.

Typos are corrected.

Formats are corrected.

source_summary:
RAN2 agreed CR to TS 36.331 in R2-1913059, which defines IE called highSpeedEnhMeasFlag2. If this field is present, the UE shall apply the high speed (500 km/h) measurement enhancements. 

In the existing timing requirements in section 7.1.2 the place holders for the high speed enhanced flag (TBD) to support speed up to 500 km/hour is replaced by the IE, “highSpeedEnhMeasFlag2”.

frozen_records.summaryOfChange:
Introducing TFirstSSB_MAX:

TFirstSSB_MAX: Is the time to first SSB indicated by the SMTC after n + THARQ+3ms, further fulfilling:
In FR1, in case of intra-band SCell activation, the occasion when all active serving cells and SCells being activated or released are transmitting SSB bursts in the same slot; in case of inter-band SCell activation, the first occasion when the SCell being activated is transmitting SSB burst.
In FR2, the occasion when all active serving cells and SCells being activated or released are transmitting SSB bursts in the same slot.
Updating corresponding requirements:

If the SCell is known and belongs to FR1, Tactivation_time is:
-	TFirstSSB+ 5ms, if the SCell measurement cycle is equal to or smaller than 160ms.
-	TFirstSSB_MAX + Trs + 5ms, if the SCell measurement cycle is larger than 160ms.
If the SCell is unknown and belongs to FR1, Tactivation_time is:
-	TFirstSSB_MAX + TSMTC_MAX + 2*Trs + 5ms provided the SCell can be successfully detected on the first attempt.

In FR1, in case of intra-band SCell activation, the occasion when all active serving cells and SCells being activated or released are transmitting SSB bursts in the same slot; in case of inter-band SCell activation, the first occasion when the SCell being activated is transmitting SSB burst.
In FR2, the occasion when all active serving cells and SCells being activated or released are transmitting SSB bursts in the same slot.
Updating corresponding requirements:

If the SCell is known and belongs to FR1, Tactivation_time is:
-	TFirstSSB+ 5ms, if the SCell measurement cycle is equal to or smaller than 160ms.
-	TFirstSSB_MAX + Trs + 5ms, if the SCell measurement cycle is larger than 160ms.
If the SCell is unknown and belongs to FR1, Tactivation_time is:
-	TFirstSSB_MAX + TSMTC_MAX + 2*Trs + 5ms provided the SCell can be successfully detected on the first attempt.

members.name: R4-1915292 CR to 38.101-2-g10 Corrections to maximum output power reduction for power class 3.docx

source_summary:
Change of MPR narrow definition as “MPRnarrow = 2.5 dB, when the allocated RB size is less than or equal to 4.32 MHz, and 0 ≤ RBstart < Ceil(1/3 NRB) or Ceil(2/3NRB) ≤ RBstart ≤ NRB-LCRB, otherwise MPRnarrow = 0 dB when RB size is greater than 4.32 MHz, where NRB is the maximum transmission bandwidth configuration defined in Table 5.3.2-1.”
Change MPR equations as “RBStart,Low = max(1, LCRB), where max() indicates the largest value of all arguments.
RBStart,High = NRB - RBStart,Low - LCRB,
An RB allocation belonging to table 6.2.2.3-1 is a Region 1 inner RB allocation if:
RBStart,Low  ≤  RBStart ≤  RBStart,High, and LCRB ≤  ceil(NRB/3), where ceil(x) is the smallest integer greater than or equal to x.
An RB allocation is an Edge allocation if it is NOT a Region 1 inner allocation.”

source_summary:
The following changes are made:
New limits for BS type 1-O and BS type 2-O are introduced, where the limits are based on Category B TX spurious emission limits. 
For BS Type 2-O, it is also clarified that the OTA RX spurious emissions requirement shall apply during the transmitter OFF period only.
A table with step frequencies is introduced.
A temporary note for stricter limits in regional regulation is added.

source_summary:
Clause 6.2D.1:
1. remove the ambiguity on applicability of the requirements when TPMI = 0 is sent:  requirements for both single-layer and dual-layer transmission is specified with two ports configured.
2. specify the fall-back single-antenna port behaviour: at least PC3 performance must be met when PUSCH is scheduled for single port transmission by DCI 0_0 (verified per connector)
3. add a requirement that full power shall according to the power class shall be delivered when PUSCH is scheduled by DCI 0_1 and the UE is configured with a single antenna port following 38.213.

The behavour according to items 2 and 3 are specified in the remaining subclauses of 6.2D. 

The requirements on unwanted emissions are specified as the total of the emissions from UE antenna ports (connectors).
